description: Masala Chai is a quintessential Indian beverage, a delightful blend of strong black tea brewed with aromatic spices and milk. This comforting drink offers a warm, invigorating experience with its rich flavor profile and fragrant aroma, perfect for any time of day. Enjoy the authentic taste of India with every sip of this beloved spiced milk tea.

ingredients.notes: Assam or Darjeeling tea works best

instructions.title: Prepare the Spices
instructions.text: Lightly crush the green cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, cloves, and black peppercorns using a mortar and pestle or the back of a spoon. Grate or thinly slice the fresh ginger.

instructions.title: Boil Water and Spices
instructions.text: In a saucepan, combine 2 cups of water with the crushed spices and grated ginger. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil over medium-high heat.

instructions.title: Add Tea Leaves
instructions.text: Once the water is boiling and the spices are fragrant, add the black tea leaves to the saucepan. Reduce the heat to medium-low and let it simmer for 2-3 minutes, allowing the tea to brew and infuse with the spices.

instructions.title: Introduce Milk and Sugar
instructions.text: Pour in the 2 cups of milk and add sugar to your desired sweetness. Stir well to combine. Increase the heat slightly and bring the chai mixture to a gentle boil.

instructions.title: Simmer and Develop Flavor
instructions.text: Once the chai starts to boil, reduce the heat to low and let it simmer gently for another 5-7 minutes. Stir occasionally to prevent the milk from scorching at the bottom. The longer it simmers, the stronger and more robust the flavors will become.

instructions.title: Strain and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the saucepan from the heat. Place a fine-mesh strainer over serving cups and carefully pour the chai through the strainer to separate the liquid from the tea leaves and spices. Serve hot and enjoy your authentic Masala Chai!

tips: For a stronger flavor, gently bruise the cardamom pods, cinnamon, and cloves before adding them to the water. This releases more of their essential oils.
Adjust the amount of ginger and black peppercorns according to your preference for spice and warmth. You can also add a pinch of nutmeg or star anise for extra complexity.
Always strain the chai immediately after simmering to prevent it from becoming too bitter from over-steeping the tea leaves. Serve hot for the best experience.
